chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah Yunus informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qarashi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yunus ibn Ribat, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah saying: 'Indeed, the people of the truth have always been in distress, but that is for a short period and a long relief.' And Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda informed us, from one of his men, who said: Ali ibn Ishaq al-Kindi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Ribat, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying, and he mentioned the same.'
Indeed, the people of the truth have always been in distress, but that is for a short period and a long relief.
ai.seo_question: What is the nature and duration of the distress experienced by the people of truth according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In the context of the Major Occultation, Imam al-Sadiq (as) reassures the Shia community that their historical endurance of persecution is a prelude to the imminent rise of al-Qa'im, transforming current tribulation into a long era of divine relief. This narration underscores the theological concept of 'subr' (patience) as a defining characteristic of the faithful during the period of waiting, linking their spiritual resilience directly to the eschatological victory of the Twelfth Imam.

en.abdullah-al-shahin:
(4) Abdul Wahid bin Abdullah bin Yunus narrated from Muhammad bin Ja’far al-Qarashi from Muhammad bin al-Husayn bin Abul Khattab from Muhammad bin Sinan from Yunus bin Ribat that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said: “The followers of the truth have always been in distress, but their distress lasts for a short time and their good end will last forever.” 

And Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa‘eed ibn ‘Uqda narrated to us from one of his narrators. He said, Ali ibn Ishaq al-Kindi narrated to us, who said, Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us from Yunus ibn Ribat, who said, "I heard Abu Abdullah (a.s) saying," and he mentioned the same."'
